funder: Paul Mellon Centre for Studies in British Art
title: Research Project Grants
amount_raw: The grants are for any amount up to £40;000.
eligibility_summary:
Any organisation, institution or nonprofit; collaborative applications welcomed. One Research Project Grant per organisation per round. Applicants must show how the funding contributes to a defined outcome or significantly to a larger research project.

All applicants must demonstrate how the award will enhance their research project on British art, visual culture and/or architecture. More information on this is available on our Our Funding Focus webpage and we have also highlighted some of our previously funded projects here.
summary: Flexible support for organisations undertaking ambitious and sustained research in British art; no set project duration, but an outcome is normally expected within five years.
notes: Own page banner 'Open for applications' + 'Applications for the Autumn 2026 round of funding are now open, applications close on Monday 14 September.' The hub (grants-and-fellowships.html) and the organisations listing (grants-organisations.html) both confirm the 14 September close for the whole Autumn 2026 round. Year 2026 for the deadline is stated on the hub ('Autumn 2026 round'). Tagged restricted for the one-application-per-organisation-per-round cap. amount_raw semicolon substitutes for the comma in '£40,000'.

funder: Paul Mellon Centre for Studies in British Art
title: Exhibition Publication Grants
amount_raw: The grants are for any amount up to £6;000.
eligibility_summary:
Any organisation, institution or non-profit. The exhibition the publication is based on may be forthcoming or may already have taken place.

We champion original research that deepens our understanding of British art and its histories, supporting projects that are rigorous in their methodologies and which intend to contribute meaningfully to scholarship.
We aim to support a wide range of individuals and organisations, recognising that fostering and putting into dialogue different perspectives enriches and develops the field.
We believe that research thrives through dialogue and shared endeavours. Our funding programme encourages connections, networks and dissemination to help advance knowledge of British art.
summary: Grants towards the costs of exhibition publications showcasing new and original research on British art.
notes: Own page 'Open for applications'; Autumn 2026 round closing Monday 14 September 2026, as for all PMC organisation grants.

funder: Paul Mellon Centre for Studies in British Art
title: Event Support Grants
amount_raw: The grants are for any amount up to £3;000.
eligibility_summary:
Any organisation, institution or nonprofit; collaborative applications welcomed. Events are expected to take place within the year of the award.

All applicants must demonstrate how the grant will enhance their event on British art, visual culture and/or architecture.

Supported event types include lectures, conferences, workshops, gallery talks, symposia and seminars. Events such as film screenings or artistic performances may qualify if accompanied by research-based talks or presentations. The event should be standalone or a dedicated series, rather than part of the organisation’s regular programming.
summary: Support for organisations disseminating research on British art through live, online and hybrid events and programming.
notes: Own page 'Open for applications'; Autumn 2026 round closing Monday 14 September 2026.

funder: Paul Mellon Centre for Studies in British Art
title: Conservation Grants
amount_raw: The grants are for any amount up to £25;000.
eligibility_summary:
Any organisation, institution or nonprofit undertaking a conservation research project or technical analysis leading to a research project. Items must be in public or charitable ownership and accessible to the public.

All applicants must demonstrate how the grant will support their original and innovative conservation research in the field of British art, visual culture and/or architecture.
summary:
Funding for organisations to undertake conservation research on significant works of British art in their own collections.
The support from this grant should result in a conservation research project that enhances the understanding of the object, the details of which should be provided in the final report.
notes: Own page 'Open for applications'; Autumn 2026 round closing Monday 14 September 2026. Listed on grants-organisations.html under 'Technical Grants' alongside Digitisation Grants. Tagged restricted because of the public/charitable-ownership condition on the items. NOTE the listing page says 'Grants of £25,000' (a fixed sum) while the scheme page says 'any amount up to £25,000' — the scheme page wins under the canonical-page rule.

funder: Paul Mellon Centre for Studies in British Art
title: Rome Fellowship
amount_raw: honorarium of £3,000 ... up to £8,000 ... towards replacement staff costs ... independent researcher there is an honorarium of £7,000
eligibility_summary: Scholars, researchers, curators, archivists and GLAM professionals with at least a first degree, from pre-doctoral PhD candidates to those internationally recognised in their field, with a track record of research in British art. Open to any country; fluency in English required plus competence in or willingness to engage with Italian. The project must relate to cultural contact, exchange and influence between Britain (including its historical Empire and Commonwealth) and Italy.
summary: A three-month residency at the British School at Rome with full board and accommodation paid directly by the Centre, plus an honorarium and, for the employed, replacement staff costs.
notes: Own page 'Closed for applications', next round Spring 2027 opening Monday 30 November 2026 — forthcoming, in scope. AMOUNT IS AWKWARD and both bounds are flagged: the cash value depends on employment status — an employed applicant gets a £3,000 honorarium plus up to £8,000 replacement staff costs (£11,000 max), while an independent researcher gets a £7,000 honorarium; the three months' board and accommodation at the BSR is paid in kind and unpriced. amount_min_gbp=3000 (lowest stated honorarium) and amount_max_gbp=15000 are a rough envelope only — FLAG FOR REVIEW, a reviewer may prefer to leave both blank. Related informational pages: grants-and-fellowships/british-school-at-rome and grants-and-fellowships/robert-macpherson (a film about a past Rome Fellow) — distractors, not rows.

title: New Narratives: Early Career Fellowship
amount_raw: £35,000 if taken as a one year Fellowship / £70,000 (£35,000 per year) if taken as a two year Fellowship
